# Onboarding & New-User Activation — Landscape Brief for Culprit

**Prepared 2026-08-12 · Web research brief for the onboarding/activation redesign (B-745, the Home-is-an-empty-state problem) · Frozen point-in-time evidence — do not edit; write a new brief if the base shifts.**
_Method: isolated web-research agent, six directed lanes, URL-cited throughout. Consumed by `docs/sessions/2026-08-12-onboarding-nux-ideation.md` + mock round 1 (`docs/culprit-onboarding-nux-mockups.html`)._

Framing: Culprit's structural problem is that its **setup moment** (create account, add pet) and its **aha moment** (the first Signal insight / vet report) are separated by 1–2 weeks of data accrual — exactly the window in which ~77% of average apps lose their users ([Andrew Chen, "Losing 80% of mobile users is normal"](https://andrewchen.com/new-data-shows-why-losing-80-of-your-mobile-users-is-normal-and-that-the-best-apps-do-much-better/)). The apps studied below solve this with four moves Culprit can borrow: deliver a same-session artifact of value, name the calibration period explicitly, make the empty Home teach the payoff, and let the record itself be the day-0 product. The wedge user (sent home with "track what she eats / watch for vomiting") arrives with higher intent and a clearer job than any wellness-app user — which makes several patterns *simpler* for Culprit than for Calm or Oura.

---

## 1. Wellness/health app onboarding teardowns

### Pattern 1a — Deliver felt value in the first 10 seconds, before any questions
- **Calm**: the literal first screen is "take a deep breath" on a blue gradient, held for the length of one breath — the product's value delivered before a single tap ([GoodUX/Appcues teardown](https://goodux.appcues.com/blog/calm-app-new-user-experience); flow recordings at [Page Flows](https://pageflows.com/calm/), [UI Sources](https://uisources.com/explainer/calm-onboarding)).
- **Headspace**: entire onboarding is ~1 minute — three questions, then straight into a first meditation ([GoodUX teardown](https://goodux.appcues.com/blog/headspaces-mindful-onboarding-sequence)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* the equivalent of "take a deep breath" is acknowledging the situation — "Your vet asked you to keep track. We'll make that easy." — before any form field.

### Pattern 1b — Motivation capture ("why are you here?") that visibly shapes what follows
- **Headspace** asks exactly three things: experience with meditation, "What brings you to Headspace?" (four options), and *when* you want to meditate — anchored to existing routines ("after waking up", not a clock time) — then shows a **recap screen** mirroring the answers back before the CTA ([GoodUX](https://goodux.appcues.com/blog/headspaces-mindful-onboarding-sequence); [teardown](https://tearthemdown.medium.com/product-teardown-headspace-user-onboarding-personalisation-b6effd0df1d7)).
- **Calm** uses a multi-select goal picker ("What brings you to Calm?" — sleep, stress, anxiety…) and later serves a "recommended for you based on your responses" dashboard ([GoodUX](https://goodux.appcues.com/blog/calm-app-new-user-experience)).
- **Flo** branches its entire onboarding on goal (track cycle / get pregnant / pregnancy), age, and experiments — complex enough that the team built an internal visual graph tool to manage the branching ([Flo Health engineering, "Mobile onboarding evolution"](https://medium.com/flo-health/mobile-onboarding-evolution-part-2-d7c324c348fe); [Mobbin flow](https://mobbin.com/explore/flows/4ceaac02-e25d-419e-ae7e-58ed7bd1e1e3)).
- **Whoop** asks users to pick a goal from presets ("Improve sleep," "Build muscle," "Focus on Wellness") ([Everyday Industries UX evaluation](https://everydayindustries.com/whoop-wearable-health-fitness-user-experience-evaluation/)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* one question — "What did the vet ask you to do?" (diet trial / watch a symptom / just tracking) — can route the pet-setup flow, decide which log types Home foregrounds, set the calibration copy, and pre-shape the eventual vet report. Culprit's wedge answer is more concrete than any wellness app's, and the answer should be *visibly* mirrored back (Headspace's recap screen).

### Pattern 1c — Account creation after investment, not before it
- **Calm** places email signup *after* the breath moment and goal selection — the user has already invested and received something ([GoodUX](https://goodux.appcues.com/blog/calm-app-new-user-experience)).
- **Oura**'s biggest reviewed friction point is the opposite: membership signup lands *after* purchase, before activation, and reads as "disjointed," dampening initial excitement ([Everyday Industries Oura evaluation](https://everydayindustries.com/oura-ring-onboarding-user-experience-evaluation/)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* collect the pet's name and the vet's directive first; ask for the account only when there is something worth saving (see also Guideline 5.1.1, §4).

### Pattern 1d — The first session ships a finished artifact, not a promise
- **Headspace**: the first session ends in an actual guided meditation — the core value, experienced once, on day 0.
- **Gentler Streak** (Apple Design Award 2024, Social Impact): positions itself as "a compass, a reminder to get moving, no matter what that means for you"; validates whatever the user did today ("If a 15-minute walk is what your body can do at that moment, that's great") rather than demanding a baseline first; its core insight — "Statistics are just numbers. Without knowing how to interpret them, they are meaningless… we wanted to focus on the humanity" ([Apple Behind the Design](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=3m0ht22s); [Apple newsroom](https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2024/06/apple-announces-winners-of-the-2024-apple-design-awards/); [Sketch interview](https://www.sketch.com/blog/gentler-streak/)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* the day-0 artifact is the **first logged meal rendered beautifully** — the moment the owner sees "Chicken & rice, 7:42am, finished" as a clean clinical record entry, tracking has already produced something the vet visit never had. Gentler Streak is the tonal proof that a warm, non-pushing register can win an ADA — it is the closest published benchmark to the Culprit voice.

## 2. Cold-start handling in data-accrual apps

### Pattern 2a — A *named*, deterministic calibration schedule ("what unlocks when")
- **Whoop** publishes the schedule in-app and in support docs: sleep data after night 1; the strap "calibrates" for 4 days; first Recovery score on day 4; Strain Coach unlocks day 5; Sleep Coach day 7; first Weekly Performance Assessment day 14; full baseline at day 30 ([What to Expect in Your First 30 Days](https://support.whoop.com/hc/en-us/articles/360057137353-What-to-Expect-in-Your-First-30-Days); [Recovery calibration period](https://support.whoop.com/hc/en-us/articles/360019622573-What-is-the-Recovery-calibration-period-); [Everyday Industries](https://everydayindustries.com/whoop-wearable-health-fitness-user-experience-evaluation/)).
- **Oura**: "It can take up to two weeks for the Oura App to learn your average values"; metrics like Resilience literally *reveal themselves* after a 2-week baseline; before that, an explicit on-screen message says long-term metrics are "still calibrating" ([Readiness Contributors](https://support.ouraring.com/hc/en-us/articles/360057791533-Readiness-Contributors); [How to Use the Oura App](https://support.ouraring.com/hc/en-us/articles/360058599753-How-to-Use-the-Oura-App)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* the Signal zone's building state should carry a day counter tied to a stated contract — "Signal is watching. Patterns usually take about two weeks of logs to show" — and named unlocks (first trend chart at N days, first Signal insight when the engine's floors are met, vet report any time). Deterministic language ("day 5 of ~14") converts dead time into anticipation. Caution: unlike Whoop, Culprit must never phrase pre-floor time as "not working yet" — the record is already valuable on day 1 (it *is* the vet report's raw material).

### Pattern 2b — Provisional value from population priors while the personal baseline builds
- **Oura**: "before your baseline is fully established, some of the guidance is based more on averages for a person of the same age and gender as you" ([Everyday Industries](https://everydayindustries.com/oura-ring-onboarding-user-experience-evaluation/); [Oura support](https://support.ouraring.com/hc/en-us/articles/360057791533-Readiness-Contributors)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* the analog is **educational, species-specific content**, not provisional verdicts — "For cats on an elimination diet, the patterns vets look for are X and Y" is safe day-2 content; a provisional "she seems fine so far" is forbidden by the n=1-never-reassures invariant. Borrow the *slot* (something in the Signal zone from day 0), not the mechanism (population-normed scoring).

### Pattern 2c — Backfill to compress the cold start
- **Flo** explicitly asks new users to "add your periods for the last 12 months, or at least the last three cycles," and sets the expectation that predictions "take a few cycles" otherwise ([Flo accuracy page](https://flo.health/flo-accuracy); [Flo help — checking predictions](https://help.flo.health/hc/en-us/articles/4406826523284-Checking-your-cycle-predictions)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* the wedge user usually has *recent history in their head* ("she's vomited three times this month; the vet visit was Tuesday"). An onboarding step — "Add anything you remember from the last couple of weeks, roughly is fine" — seeds the timeline, moves the Signal floor closer, and makes Home non-empty in minute one. (Dated-membership semantics already exist in the diet-trial model; backfilled events would need honest low-precision timestamps.)

### Pattern 2d — Per-sample value carries the user while longitudinal value accrues
- **Levels (CGM)**: user research found patients "start strong but lose engagement by week two"; the killer failure was splitting food logs and glucose data so users "can't connect cause and effect" — the fix was one unified surface where each meal immediately shows its own glucose response ([Levels blog on the patient app](https://www.levels.com/blog/patient-app-scalable-cgm-care); month-one user account at [Blue Sky Mind](https://www.ablueskymind.com/blog/levels-health-review)).
- **Whoop** gives sleep data after the *first night* even though Recovery needs 4 days ([support](https://support.whoop.com/hc/en-us/articles/360057137353-What-to-Expect-in-Your-First-30-Days)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* Culprit already has per-sample value shipped (photo AI reads on vomit/stool, the rendered log itself, Today zone). The cold-start design job is to *foreground* those in week one so the week-2 cliff Levels measured never arrives — the intelligence surface is late, but the record surface is instant.

## 3. Empty states and activation checklists

### Pattern 3a — The three NN/g jobs of an empty state
NN/g's guidelines: (1) communicate system status, (2) provide learning cues, (3) offer direct pathways into the task; and bluntly — "Do not default to totally empty states. This approach creates confusion for users, who may be left wondering if the system is still loading… or if errors have occurred" ([NN/g, Designing Empty States in Complex Applications](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/empty-state-interface-design/); [video version](https://www.nngroup.com/videos/empty-states-in-application-design-guidelines/)). Samuel Hulick's framing: "Your product is a place of activity… Many products miss a giant opportunity by simply reporting 'there's nothing to see here'" ([Appcues interview](https://www.appcues.com/blog/onboarding-new-users-an-interview-with-samuel-hulick); [UserOnboard pattern page](https://www.useronboard.com/onboarding-ux-patterns/empty-states/)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* every earned surface (Signal, Trend, report) needs a designed first-use state that says what it will become, why, and when — Principle 5 ("empty states are features") is the same rule; the gap is that Home's *composition* of empty zones was never designed as one screen.

### Pattern 3b — Ghost/preview content that shows the payoff's real shape
- **Ghost rows**: "replacing the centered illustration-and-button layout with a ghost row — a low-opacity version of what a populated row would look like, with a CTA inline… the user immediately understands the structure of the page" ([72technologies empty-states playbook](https://www.72technologies.com/blog/empty-states-as-onboarding-surface)).
- **Basecamp** pre-populates fake projects "so that you'll know where the projects will be and how they'll look" (Hulick, [Appcues interview](https://www.appcues.com/blog/onboarding-new-users-an-interview-with-samuel-hulick)).
- **Linear** starts new workspaces with a few preloaded issues ([Product Onboarding — Linear](https://productonboarding.com/companies/linear)); **Loggly** offers "populate demo data" as an explicit safe-exploration path ([NN/g](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/empty-state-interface-design/)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* the single highest-leverage borrow — a **clearly-labeled example Signal card and a one-page example vet report** ("Example — this is what two weeks of logs turns into") shown in the building state. It converts "empty" into "pending," and it advertises the wedge payoff (the report) on day 0. Labeling must be unmistakable; a sample insight that could be misread as a real read of *this* pet is a clinical-guardrails violation.

### Pattern 3c — Setup checklists: powerful, but consumer-safe only in a specific shape
- **Superhuman** turned onboarding steps into unskippable full-screen panels with smart defaults, raising completion from ~30% to 98%+; every checklist item had a one-tap CTA and moments of celebration ([Gaurav Vohra, "Obsessing Over Onboarding"](https://substack.gauravvohra.com/p/obsessing-over-onboarding-for-10); the famous concierge version at [First Round Review](https://review.firstround.com/superhuman-onboarding-playbook/)).
- **Checklist vs tour**: a checklist is "a persistent, non-linear widget showing activation tasks users complete at their own pace" — right for users who know their goal; tours are for UI orientation ([Chameleon, Onboarding UX Patterns](https://www.chameleon.io/blog/onboarding-ux-patterns)).
- Consumer apps that defer signup and let users sample content first see activation lifts of 10–30%; checklists read enterprise-y when they demand multi-step configuration upfront and feel like obligation ([UXCam examples roundup](https://uxcam.com/blog/10-apps-with-great-user-onboarding/); [Plotline examples](https://www.plotline.so/blog/mobile-app-onboarding-examples)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* don't ship "Complete your setup (2/5)." Ship a **care-plan framing of the same mechanics** — "Sadie's first week: log her meals today · add anything unusual when it happens · in about two weeks, Signal starts looking for patterns." Same progress structure, but the subject is the pet, not the app's configuration.

### Pattern 3d — Progressive disclosure / earned reveals
- **Linear** surfaces keyboard shortcuts and the command palette only weeks in, when usage patterns show readiness ([SaaSUI writeup](https://www.saasui.design/blog/saas-onboarding-flows-that-actually-convert-2026)); **Oura** reveals Resilience only after its 2-week baseline exists ([Oura support](https://support.ouraring.com/hc/en-us/articles/360058599753-How-to-Use-the-Oura-App)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* the Signal already works this way by necessity; make the *reveal an event* (the notification foundation's Day Summary is the natural carrier: "Signal found its first pattern — take a look") rather than letting the card silently appear.

## 4. Apple-specific guidance

### 4a — HIG on onboarding
Apple's line: "Ideally, people can understand your app or game simply by experiencing it, but if onboarding is necessary, provide a flow that's fast, fun, and optional" — teach through interaction, not slide decks of static explanation ([HIG — Onboarding](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/onboarding); [36 Insights from the HIG](https://uxplanet.org/36-insights-from-apple-human-interface-guidelines-4a5ee3a71299)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* the first log should *be* the tutorial (log a real meal during setup), not be preceded by a carousel about logging.

### 4b — Guideline 5.1.1: no forced registration for non-account features
Apps "cannot require user registration prior to allowing access to app content and features that are not associated specifically to the user"; the standard remediation is a guest path. Most 2026 rejections land on 5.1.1(i) (thin privacy policy), 5.1.1(v) (forced registration / missing in-app account deletion), and 5.1.1(iii) (signup fields the app doesn't need) ([PTKD 5.1.1 guide](https://ptkd.com/journal/guideline-5-1-1-data-collection-and-storage-fix); rejection threads: [developer.apple.com/forums/thread/688899](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/688899), [thread/681790](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/681790)). Related: since 2024, "Sign in with Apple" is no longer literally mandatory, but any app offering third-party login must offer an equivalent privacy-preserving option (name+email only, email hiding, no tracking); apps using *only their own* account system are exempt ([9to5Mac on revised Guideline 4.8](https://9to5mac.com/2024/01/27/sign-in-with-apple-rules-app-store/); [Appraysal 4.8 summary](https://appraysal.com/rules/4.8_sign_in_with_apple)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* a pet's health record is genuinely account-based (sync, sharing, report tokens), so requiring an account *to save data* is defensible — but letting the owner name the pet, answer the directive question, and see the example report before the account ask is both better UX and cheaper review insurance. Email-only auth (current setup) avoids the 4.8 obligation entirely.

### 4c — Permission timing: contextual, never a launch-time battery
NN/g: tie requests to the feature that needs them, and never interrupt mid-task ([NN/g, Mobile-App Permission Requests](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/permission-requests/)). Deferred, in-context prompts see materially higher grant rates (one industry figure: +28% vs launch-time asks — [Dogtown Media guide](https://www.dogtownmedia.com/the-ask-when-and-how-to-request-mobile-app-permissions-camera-location-contacts/); [Branch on iOS opt-in](https://www.branch.io/resources/blog/best-practices-user-opt-in-ios-14/)). Purpose strings must be specific ([Apple Tech Talk, "Write clear purpose strings"](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/110152/)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* camera permission belongs at the first photo log, not onboarding; this matches the shipped photo pipeline and costs nothing.

### 4d — Notifications: primer first, and consider provisional authorization
Best practice is a two-step ask: an in-app pre-permission primer explaining the specific value, and the system dialog only after the user says yes to the primer — because a declined system prompt is nearly unrecoverable ([OneSignal prompt docs](https://documentation.onesignal.com/docs/en/prompt-for-push-permissions); [Hurree, iOS push best practices](https://blog.hurree.co/ios-push-notification-permissions-best-practises)). iOS **provisional authorization** delivers quietly to Notification Center with no prompt at all, letting the app *demonstrate* 2–3 valuable notifications before asking for full opt-in ([Nil Coalescing on trial notifications](https://nilcoalescing.com/blog/TrialNotificationsWithProvisionalAuthorizationOnIOS/); ["Stop Asking Permission on Day One"](https://medium.com/@shobhakartiwari/ios-push-notifications-stop-asking-permission-on-day-one-7a2fb2bbe366)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* the B-661 consent/primer flow already matches best practice; the onboarding-specific addition is *timing* — the natural ask is the moment the owner sets a tracking directive ("Want a quiet evening reminder while the trial runs?"), which is a consented tool under the ratified D1 carve-out, not a nudge.

### 4e — Paywalls at first launch
A hard paywall contradicting free-app store metadata violates accurate-metadata expectations (2.3.1); paywalls must state price, period, auto-renewal and cancellation clearly (3.1.2 rejections spiked in early 2026 over confusing trial toggles); and the "close the paywall, pop a discount offer" pattern draws rejections ([RevenueCat, ultimate rejection guide](https://www.revenuecat.com/blog/growth/the-ultimate-guide-to-app-store-rejections); [RevenueFlo on paywall rejections](https://revenueflo.com/blog/common-ios-paywall-rejections-and-the-fixes-that-work); [Apple forum thread on the one-time-offer rejection](https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/768912)). Calm and Flo both interpose trial-paywall screens between signup and first content — the acknowledged highest-drop-off screen in Calm's own flow ([GoodUX](https://goodux.appcues.com/blog/calm-app-new-user-experience)).
- *Applies to Culprit:* Pets > $ already forbids the Calm/Flo interposition; this section is ammunition for keeping the B-251 paywall mock *out* of the critical path permanently.

## 5. Pet-care app space

Published teardowns are thin here — itself a finding: **no pet app has a documented, deliberately-designed activation flow**, and none designs for the "vet sent me home with a directive" moment.

- **Pawfolio** (closest feature-set competitor): first-run is "a smooth, interactive walkthrough of the app" plus "clearer Premium+ trial messaging" — i.e., a feature tour and an early upsell, with reminders/schedules as the hook ([pawfolio.app](https://www.pawfolio.app/); [App Store listing](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/pawfolio-pet-tracker-care/id6743056578)). No motivation capture, no cold-start framing.
- **DogLog**: explicitly markets the sick-pet job ("log symptoms… share activity and symptom data with your vet") and multi-caregiver logging, but reviewers note no intelligence layer of any kind — "a solid daily log but not a complete health management solution"; dog-only ([doglogapp.com](https://www.doglogapp.com/); [ElevenApril comparison](https://elevenapril.com/blog/best-pet-journal-apps)).
- **11pets**: deep record-keeping and vet-sharing, but "the interface feels dated… no health scoring," heavy manual setup upfront ([ElevenApril](https://elevenapril.com/blog/best-pet-journal-apps); [Woofz roundup](https://www.woofz.com/blog/6-top-dog-health-tracker-apps/)).
- **Whistle** (hardware): the strongest pet onboarding reviewed — "setup takes all of five minutes," then a "daily check-in" card gives day-one value from passive data ([SafeWise review](https://www.safewise.com/blog/whistle-3-gps-dog-tracker-review/); [Gearbrain](https://www.gearbrain.com/review-whistle-go-explore-tracker-2640162695.html)) — but the data is passive; there is no logging habit to build.
- **PetDesk** is B2B2C vet-clinic communication (records, reminders, two-way texting), onboarded via the clinic over 3–4 weeks — not a consumer activation model, but a reminder that the *vet channel* is a distribution wedge ([Software Advice reviews](https://www.softwareadvice.com/veterinary/petdesk-profile/reviews/)).

**Gaps a clinical-grade tracker can beat:** (1) every competitor onboards to *the app* (tour of features) instead of to *the pet's situation*; (2) none sets expectations for when tracking pays off — the record is its own reward or nothing; (3) none previews a vet-facing artifact, despite "share with your vet" being the marquee claim; (4) upsell arrives before value (Pawfolio) — the exact anti-pattern Pets > $ already bans; (5) tone is utility-grade, nowhere near the Calm/Gentler Streak register. Culprit's directive-first onboarding + example-report preview would be category-unique on all five.

## 6. Activation concepts, precisely named

- **Setup / Aha / Habit moments** (Reforge): the setup moment is "when the user has completed the actions required to receive value"; the aha moment is the first *experience* of value — "concrete and describable in one sentence, or you have not defined it"; the habit moment is when a recurring trigger→value loop closes without deliberation ([Reforge — Defining Your Aha Moment](https://www.reforge.com/c/retention-series-eg/activation/aha-moment); [Define your setup moment](https://www.reforge.com/guides/define-your-setup-moment); summary at [GrowthPigeon](https://growthpigeon.com/articles/setup-aha-habit-saas-activation-moments)).
- **Aha vs activation metric**: aha is the cognitive shift ("I need this"); the activation metric is the measurable behavioral proxy that predicts retention — canonical examples: Facebook's 7 friends in 10 days, Slack's 2,000 team messages ([Appcues, aha-moment examples](https://www.appcues.com/blog/aha-moment-examples)).
- **Time to first value (TTFV/TTV)**: the clock from signup to first meaningful result; shortening it is the core onboarding lever ([Appcues, Time to Value](https://www.appcues.com/blog/time-to-value)).
- **Day 0/1/7/30 retention framing**: ~77% of users abandon an average app within 3 days; D1 60% / D7 30% / D30 15% is a *good* curve ([Andrew Chen](https://andrewchen.com/new-data-shows-why-losing-80-of-your-mobile-users-is-normal-and-that-the-best-apps-do-much-better/); [Amplitude benchmarking method](https://medium.com/permutable-analytics/how-to-calculate-benchmark-day-1-day-7-and-day-30-retention-in-amplitude-analytics-d500a77eae04)).
- **"The empty state is the product"** (Samuel Hulick / UserOnboard): "Empty states are the very definition of integrated — they're literally part of your product whether you design for them or not" ([UserOnboard](https://www.useronboard.com/onboarding-ux-patterns/empty-states/); [Appcues interview](https://www.appcues.com/blog/onboarding-new-users-an-interview-with-samuel-hulick)).

**Mapped to Culprit:** setup = account + pet + directive; the true aha (first Signal insight) is structurally 1–2 weeks out — so Culprit needs a **proxy aha inside session one** (the first rendered log + the example report: "my chaos is becoming a clinical document") and should define its **activation metric** as something like *N events logged across ≥3 distinct days in week one* — the behavior that both predicts habit and feeds the Signal floor. The day-3 abandonment cliff lands squarely inside the calibration window, which is why §2's expectation-setting patterns are not polish but survival.

---

## (a) Shortlist — patterns most worth adopting

1. **Directive-first motivation capture.** One onboarding question — "What did the vet ask you to do?" — routes setup, Home composition, calibration copy, and report framing; mirror the answer back Headspace-style. ([Headspace](https://goodux.appcues.com/blog/headspaces-mindful-onboarding-sequence), [Flo](https://medium.com/flo-health/mobile-onboarding-evolution-part-2-d7c324c348fe))
2. **First log inside onboarding.** The tutorial *is* logging one real meal; TTFV collapses to minute one. ([HIG — teach by doing](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/onboarding))
3. **Backfill invitation.** "Add anything you remember from the last two weeks — roughly is fine" seeds the timeline and shortens the Signal floor, Flo-style. ([Flo accuracy](https://flo.health/flo-accuracy))
4. **A named calibration period with a day counter.** "Signal is watching — day 3. Patterns usually take about two weeks of logs." Deterministic unlock language, Whoop-style, phrased so the pre-floor record is never "not working." ([Whoop first 30 days](https://support.whoop.com/hc/en-us/articles/360057137353-What-to-Expect-in-Your-First-30-Days), [Oura calibration](https://support.ouraring.com/hc/en-us/articles/360057791533-Readiness-Contributors))
5. **Example-payoff preview, unmistakably labeled.** A ghost Signal card and a one-page sample vet report ("Example") in the building state — the record's destination shown on day 0. ([72technologies ghost rows](https://www.72technologies.com/blog/empty-states-as-onboarding-surface), [NN/g](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/empty-state-interface-design/), [Basecamp via Hulick](https://www.appcues.com/blog/onboarding-new-users-an-interview-with-samuel-hulick))
6. **"First week" care-plan card in place of a setup checklist.** Checklist mechanics (persistent, per-pace, one-tap CTAs) wearing pet-care language — "Sadie's first week" — never "Complete your setup (2/5)." ([Chameleon](https://www.chameleon.io/blog/onboarding-ux-patterns), [Superhuman completion data](https://substack.gauravvohra.com/p/obsessing-over-onboarding-for-10))
7. **Per-sample value foregrounded in week one.** Photo AI reads and the beautifully rendered log carry days 0–13, the Levels lesson (cause-and-effect visible per event, one unified surface). ([Levels](https://www.levels.com/blog/patient-app-scalable-cgm-care))
8. **Educational species-specific content in the Signal slot.** "What vets look for during a diet trial" fills the intelligence surface safely before data exists — the safe analog of Oura's population-prior guidance. ([Oura](https://everydayindustries.com/oura-ring-onboarding-user-experience-evaluation/))
9. **Value before account; contextual permissions; primer-gated notifications.** Pet + directive before signup (5.1.1 insurance); camera at first photo; the notification ask at directive-setup, primer first — provisional authorization as the soft path. ([PTKD 5.1.1](https://ptkd.com/journal/guideline-5-1-1-data-collection-and-storage-fix), [NN/g permissions](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/permission-requests/), [OneSignal](https://documentation.onesignal.com/docs/en/prompt-for-push-permissions))
10. **Make the first Signal reveal an event.** When the first insight exists, announce it (Day Summary notification: "Signal found its first pattern") — the Oura/Linear earned-reveal, celebrated once, calmly. ([Oura reveals](https://support.ouraring.com/hc/en-us/articles/360058599753-How-to-Use-the-Oura-App), [Linear](https://www.saasui.design/blog/saas-onboarding-flows-that-actually-convert-2026))

## (b) Anti-patterns to explicitly avoid

1. **Streaks, guilt loops, and urgency mechanics.** Besides the register mismatch (benchmarks are Calm/Oura/Gentler Streak, whose ADA was won on the *opposite* stance — [Apple](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=3m0ht22s)), a streak on a *clinical record* creates an incentive to fabricate logs to keep the chain — corrupting the very data the vet report depends on. Gentler Streak proves warm > pushy retains ("unusually high open and return rates").
2. **Paywall or trial interposed in the first run.** Calm's own teardown flags its trial screen as the likeliest drop-off point ([GoodUX](https://goodux.appcues.com/blog/calm-app-new-user-experience)); Pawfolio leads with Premium trial messaging before value; and unclear first-launch paywalls are an active 3.1.2 rejection magnet ([RevenueFlo](https://revenueflo.com/blog/common-ios-paywall-rejections-and-the-fixes-that-work)). For Culprit it also violates Pets > $ outright.
3. **Launch-time permission battery (notifications + camera at first open).** Measurably lower grant rates, and a declined iOS prompt is near-unrecoverable ([NN/g](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/permission-requests/), [Branch](https://www.branch.io/resources/blog/best-practices-user-opt-in-ios-14/)). Every ask must arrive attached to the feature that needs it.
4. **The bare "No data yet" empty state — and its evil twin, the falsely reassuring one.** A blank Home reads as broken ([NN/g: "do not default to totally empty states"](https://www.nngroup.com/articles/empty-state-interface-design/)); but equally, a building state must never imply wellness ("all quiet — looking good") — absence of data is not absence of disease (the n=1 invariant). The building state says what's being watched *for* and when it will resolve, never how the pet is doing.
5. **Feature-tour carousels and multi-screen app walkthroughs.** The pet category's default (Pawfolio's "interactive walkthrough") and the HIG's named anti-pattern — onboarding should be "fast, fun, and optional," taught through the first real log, not slides about zones and tabs ([HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/onboarding); [Pawfolio](https://www.pawfolio.app/)). Every tour screen is a screen between the vet's directive and the first logged meal.
